mainstream.fact: The African National Congress is on course to lose most of South Africa's major cities in Wednesday's local elections, Semafor Africa reports, with its support now concentrated in small towns and rural provinces. The vote decides who runs more than 250 municipalities, which provide water, sanitation and refuse collection, and is the ANC's first nationwide test since it had to form a coalition in 2024.

opinion.text: a poor result could force the ANC to treat the Democratic Alliance as an equal power in policy-making.

top.claude: Markets are pricing words, not a deal: Goldman raising its forecast on the day the price fell shows how fragile the drop is. The real test comes once Trump no longer needs calm before a vote.
top.fact: Brent crude fell about 6% on Monday to around $106 a barrel after Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Trump would like to end the Iran war diplomatically and Iranian leaders said they were weighing a proposal that would soon reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar-mediated talks continued, but Trump also said Washington still has one or two targets in Iran to take care of, and at a Gulf summit in Bahrain regional states voiced fear of renewed fighting after the midterms. Goldman Sachs raised its average oil price forecasts for this year and next.

opinion.text: Iran has no election to worry about, so it can absorb pressure, play for time and frustrate Washington's push for a quick deal.

top.claude: Both sides now claim the constitution and reject each other's judges, so every future ruling can be contested, a precedent that is hard to undo.
top.fact: On Friday evening seven judges of Poland's Constitutional Tribunal suspended its president, Bogdan Święczkowski, accusing him of complicity in President Karol Nawrocki's refusal to swear in judges chosen by parliament. Nawrocki turned his plane back mid-flight to Senegal and joined protesters outside the court, calling it a coup, while Prime Minister Donald Tusk says he is restoring the rule of law. Police were deployed at the court, which has lost its quorum, and protests continued over the weekend.

opinion.text: both camps have dirty hands, since the centrists tried to pack the court in 2015 before the populists turned it into an enabler.
